intro_html: Jamaican jerk is a seasoning and a cooking method, and the seasoning is the part that travels. Allspice, thyme, cinnamon, nutmeg and heat go onto the chicken, then the whole thing cooks down over rice and peas made the island way, with coconut milk and kidney beans in the pot. It is the single richest bowl in this batch at 751 calories and 51 grams of protein, and it costs about $3.46 (at everyday cost). One pot, one lid, no side dishes to think about.
cost_closing_html: About $3.46 a bowl (at everyday cost) for the biggest, heaviest dinner in this batch. Coconut milk and chicken are the two lines that matter and everything else rounds to loose change.
shop_smart: Coconut milk is the second biggest line. Buy the store brand cans in the international aisle, check for full fat, and buy several when they go on sale because the cans last a year on a shelf.

Canned kidney beans are what Jamaicans call peas in rice and peas, and they are one of the cheapest sources of anything in the store. Two cans covers the batch. Dried beans are cheaper still if you plan the soak.

Jerk seasoning is worth mixing yourself. Allspice, cinnamon, nutmeg, cayenne, thyme, garlic powder and brown sugar are all things you probably own already, and a jar of premixed jerk costs more than all of them combined.
Green onions and jalapeno are the fresh heat. Buy them the day you cook, since scallions wilt fast and a soft jalapeno has no snap left in it.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Rub the chicken thighs with the jerk seasoning, dried thyme, paprika, cajun seasoning, salt and black pepper. Let them sit at least 30 minutes, or overnight in the fridge if you have the time.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large heavy oven-safe pot over medium-high and sear the thighs in batches until the seasoning darkens and sticks. Set them aside; they finish later.
Cook the diced onion in the same pot for 4 minutes, then add the garlic, the minced jalapeno and the bay leaves and cook one more minute.
Stir in the rice and the drained kidney beans and toast for two minutes so the grains take on the jerk fond off the bottom.
Pour in the coconut milk and chicken broth, scrape the pot clean, and bring it to a boil. Lay the chicken back on top with any juices.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest burner setting, or in a 350F oven, for 25 to 30 minutes until the rice is tender and the chicken reads 165F. Rest it covered another 10 minutes off the heat.
Pull the bay leaves, chop the chicken, fold everything together in your mixing pot, and finish with the sliced green onions.
portion_html: Set the loaded pot on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight, and divide by 14. That number goes in every container. Each one carries 751 calories, which makes this the bowl to grab on a day you actually worked for it.

steps: Rub the chicken thighs with jerk seasoning, thyme, paprika and cajun seasoning and rest 30 minutes.
Sear the thighs in oil in batches, then soften onion, garlic, jalapeno and bay leaves in the same pot.
Toast the rice and drained kidney beans in the pot fond.
Add coconut milk and broth, top with the chicken, cover, and cook 25 to 30 minutes until the rice is tender.
Rest 10 minutes, chop the chicken, fold in green onions, and portion into 14 containers.
